answer: A whisper is not proof, so the network samples voices instead. Each identity must be named by two holders whose karst records predate it, and one naming serves one identity, so n aliases need n separate namers and cannot replay a single introduction. Every name is written with a quill that records its writer, and the k-th naming an operator files costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated voices. An audit re-asks a random namer; a naming that cannot be confirmed erases the whole karst hollow and its bonds.
